title: Detect config drift between intended Dedicated pool config and actual cluster/runtime settings
creator: Vanessa Ortiz
project: Provision-to-ready automation sprint (Dedicated Capacity & Fleet Management)
description:
Problem
During the staging pilot we saw multiple cases where the pool's *intended* configuration (validated JSON config + pinned chart/runtime versions) did not match what was *actually running* in the cluster. These drift cases were a root cause of:
- "Bootstrapping stuck" due to helm values/overrides getting manually tweaked to recover a prior issue
- perf-canary inconsistencies (batching/cache flags not matching intended defaults)
- confusing operator experience: control plane says Ready, but nodes are running non-standard settings

Goal
Add an automated config drift detection mechanism that compares intended pool config vs observed cluster/runtime settings, stores a drift summary, and surfaces it in the Dedicated readiness dashboard and control plane API.

Non-goals
- No real-time enforcement/auto-remediation in this ticket (we only detect + surface).
- We will not diff secrets material (KMS references only, never raw values).
- We are not attempting to detect every possible k8s-level drift; focus on the settings that map to known outages/perf regressions.

Definition: "Intended" vs "Observed"
Intended:
- The validated pool config snapshot stored by the control plane at provisioning time (post-schema validation, including resolved defaults).
- Includes pinned runtime/helm chart versions and a normalized set of effective values used for bootstrap.

Observed:
- Helm release metadata (chart version + values for runtime-related charts)
- K8s objects that affect scheduling/runtime behavior (node labels/taints used by dedicated pools, runtime daemonset env vars, configmaps)
- Runtime settings exposed via our runtime "/healthz/config" endpoint (subset only; needs to be safe to expose)

Proposed approach
1) Canonicalization
- Implement a canonical representation for drift comparison ("drift keys"), to avoid false positives from ordering/defaulting.
- Examples of drift keys:
  - runtime.chart.version
  - runtime.values.batch.max_tokens
  - runtime.values.kv_cache.enabled
  - runtime.values.quantization.profile
  - routing.registration.pool_id (sanity only)
  - node.labels.redwood.ai/pool
  - node.taints.redwood.ai/dedicated
  - autoscaling.guardrails.max_nodes (if available from intended config)

2) Drift detector job
- Runs as part of provisioning pipeline immediately after Validating stage completes, before marking Ready.
- Also runs periodically (e.g., every 30 minutes) for pools in Ready state to catch manual edits after handoff.
- Fetch intended config snapshot from control plane DB/API.
- Fetch observed state from cluster (kube API + helm release data) and runtime introspection endpoint.
- Compute diff and classify as:
  - none
  - warning (allowed drift or low-risk; informational)
  - critical (must page/ticket; may block Ready gating depending on field)

3) Storage + API surfacing
- Store drift summary in control plane as:
  - drift_status: none|warning|critical
  - drift_last_checked_at
  - drift_items_count
  - drift_summary (short string)
  - drift_details (pointer/ID for detailed diff stored as an event payload; avoid huge fields on pool object)
- Expose drift_status fields in pool status API used by dashboard.

4) Dashboard surfacing
- Add a "Config drift" widget to the Dedicated readiness dashboard:
  - filter by pool/customer/region
  - breakdown counts by drift_status
  - table of pools with critical drift + last_checked
  - deep link to control plane event / diff output

Operational considerations / guardrails
- Allowlist: Some fields are expected to differ across SKUs/regions (e.g., GPU driver minor patch) and should not trigger drift.
- Break-glass: If operators intentionally deviate from intended config (rare), they should do it via the audited break-glass override mechanism (ENG-2745/ENG-2751). Drift detection should still show warning, not critical, if the deviation is linked to an approved override.
- Cardinality: diff output must be bounded; emit counts + stable keys only in metrics.
- Failure modes: If drift detector cannot reach cluster (auth/network), record drift_status=warning with summary "drift check failed" and emit a structured event; do not hard-block provisioning unless we decide otherwise.

Acceptance criteria
- Drift detector runs on at least staging pilot pools and records drift_last_checked_at.
- Can detect known drift scenarios from pilot incident: helm values mismatch (batching flags) and node taint mismatch.
- Control plane API exposes drift_status and last_checked timestamp.
- Dashboard displays drift_status and allows filtering/drilldown.
- Unit/integration tests cover canonicalization and at least 2 drift diffs.

Implementation notes
- Prefer using the standardized terraform outputs and chart pinning to identify the correct cluster/namespace/release names.
- Keep drift key list small and opinionated; we can expand later.

Links
- Confluence: provision-to-ready overview (Readiness + Validating definitions)
- Linear: ENG-2745 (config schema), ENG-2749 (dashboard), ENG-2751 (manual override/pause)
- GitHub: PR for drift detection implementation will be linked here once opened.
comments: 2025-02-20 (Vanessa Ortiz): Adding this as a follow-up from the Bootstrapping incident thread. We need something that makes it obvious when clusters diverge from the config we *think* we applied; otherwise SREs chase ghosts.

2025-02-22 (Benji Okafor): Drafted drift keys list. Trying to keep it to "things that bite us": chart version, key runtime flags (batching/cache/quant), node taints/labels. Avoiding driver versions for now since it varies a lot by image patch and will be noisy.

2025-02-24 (Rafael Mendes): +1 on running it both post-validation and periodically. For gating: I'd prefer we do NOT block Ready on drift check failures (connectivity), but we should block on *critical drift* for chart version/runtime flags. Otherwise Ready loses meaning.

2025-02-25 (Aisha Bello): Please make sure drift emits metrics with bounded labels. Suggest: metric "dedicated_drift_status" with labels pool_id (maybe hashed) is too high-cardinality; better labels are region, sku, status. Pool/customer details can live in events/logs/dashboard queries.

2025-02-27 (Benji Okafor): Opened PR 48238 with initial implementation. Uses canonicalization helper to normalize values; stores summary on pool object and writes detailed diff as provisioning event payload (type=pool.drift.detected). Also added a small allowlist for known benign keys.

2025-02-28 (Miles Thornton): Review note: periodic drift job should jitter schedule per pool to avoid thundering herd when a region has many pools. Also, ensure kube API timeouts are <10s and bounded retries.

2025-03-03 (Benji Okafor): Addressed review: added jitter + timeouts. Also added mapping to break-glass overrides: if a diff matches an active override record, status=warning and summary mentions override ID.

2025-03-05 (Benji Okafor): Merged PR 48238. Dashboard surfacing is in ENG-2749 follow-up; API fields are now present. Marking Done for drift detection + storage + events. Next: tune severity mapping after first prod rollout.
